newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel lodges fraud complaint - paper.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel lodges fraud complaint - paper.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom has lodged a complaint in court charging fraud and use of forged documents in connection with reports of an alleged conversation between the current and former bosses of Alcatel's British partner, GEC, the newspaper La Tribune reported on on Monday.
Alcatel officials were not immediately available for comment.
La Tribune said a Paris civil court may appoint an investigating magistrate in the case.

Reports of a chat between former GEC chairman Lord Weinstock and his successor George Simpson in which they allegedly discussed their designs on French state companies Framatome and Thomson SA through their partnership with Alcatel circulated in the press.

Although Weinstock called the reports "a tissue of lies," Alcatel is said to believe that the reports, based on an alleged document, hurt its chances to win the bidding for Thomson during the electronics group's privatisation.
La Tribune said Alcatel believes the document was forged intentionally to hurt its chances.

The government chose Lagardere's offer for Thomson in October but pulled the plug on the privatisation last month and started from scratch after the privatisation commission said it could not approve the terms of the Lagardere offer.
